title: Augment, transfer, separate, and patchify
brief: Write a seeded crop-and-flip and a mixup that blends labels too. Count a depthwise-separable layer and match it to a full convolution. Cut an image into patches and show the embedding equals a strided convolution. Then train a linear head on frozen features.
hints: Draw top, left, and flip from the same generator in that order. Pad first with np.pad(x, pad), then cut padded[top:top + H, left:left + W]. Reverse the columns with out[:, ::-1].

With x = [[1, 0], [0, 2]], y = [[1, 0], [0, 1]], lam = 0.75, and partners swapped, the first mixed input is 0.75*[1, 0] + 0.25*[0, 2] = [0.75, 0.5], and the first mixed label is [0.75, 0.25]. Apply the same formula to x and y.
At 64 channels in and out with 3 by 3 filters, the depthwise step has 64*9 = 576 weights and the pointwise step has 64*64 = 4096, so 4672 in all against 36864 for a full layer.
Build the depthwise output first: for each window, multiply x[:, i:i+k, j:j+k] by dw and sum over the last two axes only. Then mix channels with np.tensordot(pw, mid, axes=(1, 0)).
x.reshape(C, H//p, p, W//p, p) splits both spatial axes. Transpose to (H//p, W//p, C, p, p) and reshape to (patches, C*p*p). Putting C last instead of first reads each patch in the wrong order.
patch_embed is patchify(x, p) @ kernel.reshape(D, -1).T + bias. The kernel's flattening order, (C, p, p), must match the patch's.
Append a column of ones to F, then solve (F1.T @ F1 / n + lam * I) w = F1.T @ t / n with t = 2*y - 1. Use np.linalg.solve, not an inverse.
For apply_update, build a new dict with a comprehension. A frozen name keeps a copy of its array, and every other name gets params[k] - lr * grads[k].
